subject: ACME - Procurement & Security qualification follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmecorp.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: ACME - Procurement & Security qualification follow-up

Hi Jordan — great to meet earlier today. Thanks for walking through Acme's priorities for inference (low-latency retrieval use cases + internal analytics). Quick recap and next steps so we're aligned: 

- Procurement readiness: you mentioned Acme prefers PO-based purchases and needs information on our invoicing cadence and whether we support marketplace procurement.
- Security gating: procurement will require SOC 2 Type II, an executed DPA, and answers to a short security questionnaire (they flagged data residency and audit logging).
- Commercial path: Acme is evaluating a reserved capacity / dedicated plan for predictable throughput; pricing model and term length are the open items.

Requested items I can provide this week: Redwood SOC 2 report, our standard DPA, a short playbook on Marketplace options, and an outline of the procurement paper process (PO vs. card).

Next steps:
1) I'll attach the SOC 2 and DPA and share a Drive folder with the security docs (see link).
2) Jordan — can you confirm whether procurement requires countersignature from Acme legal or if standard Redwood terms are fine? Also, whom should I loop from procurement for contract redlines?
3) I'll loop in Rishi (commercial) and Neha (contracts) to coordinate the PO vs card path and DocuSign/marketplace options.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Report_2026.pdf, Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - Procurement & Security qualification follow-up

Thanks Marissa — good call. A few clarifications from procurement on our side: 

- Commercial/payment: Acme will default to a PO process for anything > $25k/yr. For smaller pilots we can pay by corporate card. Please confirm you can invoice to a PO line and accept Net 45 terms.
- Marketplace: we prefer to procure via AWS Marketplace when available, but it's not a hard requirement. If Redwood is listed, procurement can fast-track approvals; otherwise we'll go through our SOW/PO flow.
- Security gating: SOC 2 Type II and a signed DPA are must-haves. We also have a short security questionnaire — attached is the Acme procurement checklist to indicate gating items. 

Attached: Acme_Procurement_Checklist.pdf

ACME procurement contacts for redlines: procurement@acmecorp.com and legal review led by James Lee (j.lee@acmecorp.com). Please loop them into any contract redlines.

Jordan
Director, Cloud Platforms
Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmecorp.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - Procurement & Security qualification follow-up

Jordan — appreciate the details and the checklist. Quick responses inline and proposed timeline: 

- PO & terms: We can accept Net 30 or Net 45 on PO for contract values > $25k/yr. I'll have our billing team draft invoice flow notes for your procurement team by EOD Friday.
- Marketplace: Redwood is available via AWS Marketplace in selected regions; I'll include the marketplace SKU and guidance in the Drive folder. If you want the marketplace route, we can engage partnerships to speed procurement.
- Security docs: attaching the SOC 2 report and our standard DPA now. 

Proposed next steps: 
1) I'll share a Drive folder with the SOC2, DPA, and marketplace guidance (link below).
2) Rishi — can you prepare a short commercial summary (term suggestions, pricing band for Dedicated) so Jordan can present to procurement/finance?
3) Neha — can you own the contract redline loop and upload a clean DocuSign envelope if Acme prefers electronic signature? If Acme wants marketplace, we may need to coordinate quotes via our marketplace team.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-Redwood-Acme-Security
DocuSign intent: https://www.docusign.com/link/rdw-acme-intent
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deals/95012

Thanks — attaching SOC2 + DPA.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Report_2026.pdf, Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmecorp.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - Procurement & Security qualification follow-up

Looping in as requested. Quick notes from commercial: 

- I'll draft a 12-month reserved capacity proposal with 3 pricing bands (pilot, mid, committed) and include estimated monthly token throughput and a recommended SLA. Aim to have the commercial summary by EOD Monday.
- On PO vs card: we'll include both flows in the summary and call out any billing lead time for PO activation. If Acme goes marketplace, procurement turnaround is usually faster but may affect pricing structure (marketplace fees).
- Neha — once you have the DPA/terms ready, can you open the DocuSign envelope and add James Lee (j.lee@acmecorp.com) and procurement@acmecorp.com as signers/CC?

I'll also flag this deal to our Marketplace team to confirm SKU availability for Acme's target regions.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
